observations: Photo 0: Silver-top retro-style mirrorless body with 'Nikon' and 'Zfc' engraving, rear body cap on marked 'Nikon Z mount', front cap in place.

Photo 1: Close-up of the top plate showing ISO dial (100-51200) and shutter speed markings, 'Zfc' badge visible, a manual-focus lens mounted with aperture ring markings (f2-f16 ish) and no Nikon branding on the lens itself.

Photo 2: Overhead shot showing the camera with lens attached, a separate battery marked 'Nikon', a charger marked 'Nikon Battery Charger', two rear lens/body caps, and a lens cap marked 'TTArtisan APS-C 35mm f2.0'.
No photo shows a power-on screen, menu, or software readout of shutter count.
No macro or backlit shot of the lens glass to check for fungus, haze, or scratches.
No shot of the sensor (with body cap removed) or of ports/screen functioning.
No serial number or hologram close-up on the battery or body to confirm originality.

Internal/service history cannot be judged from exterior photos.

Backlit/macro photo through the lens glass (front and rear elements) for fungus/scratch check

response.reason: The item is a Nikon Z fc with a third-party manual lens, but none of the three comparables (an older Micro Four Thirds Lumix G7, a Canon M50 with kit lens, and a full-frame flagship Nikon Z8 body) are a reasonable match in tier or mount, so no reliable cheapest/dearest pick can be made from this list.
